parameters.content:
**📘 WORKFLOW DETAILS**

Short-Line Railroad FRA Track Defect Severity Router & Tag-Out Approval Gate

Value: turns a daily track-inspection pull into an FRA-Part-213-style severity classification, a real speed-restriction/remedial-timeframe computation, and — for the segments that matter most — a supervisor approval gate before any segment is actually tagged out of service.

Who it's for: short-line and regional railroad track-maintenance departments who run daily or periodic FRA Class-of-Track inspections and need defect severity triaged consistently, with a human always in the loop before the most severe (Class 5) calls take effect.

How it works:
1. Schedule Trigger polls daily for segments due inspection.
2. Fetch Segments Due & Inspector Notes pulls each due segment's inspector notes as its own item.
3. Classify Defect Severity (Text Classifier, own Chat Model) reads the inspector's free-text notes and routes each segment into one of 4 categories: No Defect, Class 1-2 Minor, Class 3-4 Serious, Class 5 Immediate Halt.
4. Each category's own Set node stamps a defect_category field (Text Classifier itself never writes one — see the standing rule), then all 4 converge into Compute FRA Speed Restriction & Remedial Timeframe (Code), which computes a real speed restriction (mph) and remedial deadline off the track class + category.
5. Requires Immediate Tag-Out? branches: anything short of Class 5 is shaped straight to filing. A Class 5 call instead triggers Request Supervisor Tag-Out Approval — a genuine Slack send-and-wait gate.
6. Route Approval Response (3-way Switch) reads the supervisor's reply and finalizes as approved-as-recommended, approved-with-edit (supervisor's own text becomes the final action), or rejected (sent back for a field re-check).
7. Every path — non-urgent and all three approval outcomes — converges on Archive Defect Tag-Out Record, then Notify Track Supervisor & Dispatch.

Node summary: Schedule Trigger → Set (normalize) → HTTP Request (segments due) → Text Classifier+Chat Model (severity) → Set×4 (category tag) → Code (speed/remedial calc) → If (tag-out gate) → Slack send-and-wait (approval) → Switch (3-way response routing) → Set×3 (finalize outcome) / Set (non-urgent shape) → Google Drive (archive) → Slack (notify).

Input: the daily segments-due API response, one item per segment with inspector_defect_notes and track_class. Output: a Drive-archived tag-out record per segment and a Slack post to the track-ops channel.

Sticky colour legend: trigger=1 (blue), transform=2 (grey), ai=3 (yellow), branch=4 (green), storage=5 (purple), notify=6 (orange).

**⚙️ SETUP GUIDE**

Credentials required (create these exact names on import):
- "Track Inspection System API Key" (HTTP Header Auth) → Fetch Segments Due & Inspector Notes
- "OpenAI account" (OpenAI API) → Classifier Model
- "Track Ops Slack Bot" (Slack API) → both Request Supervisor Tag-Out Approval and Notify Track Supervisor & Dispatch
- "Track Compliance Google Drive account" (Google Drive OAuth2) → Archive Defect Tag-Out Record

Setup steps:
1. Import this JSON via n8n → Workflows → Import from File.
2. Create/select the 3 credentials above on their nodes.
3. Replace the placeholder URL in Fetch Segments Due & Inspector Notes with your real track-inspection system endpoint (must return one record per segment with segment_id, track_class, inspector_defect_notes).
4. Set REPLACE_WITH_TRACK_OPS_CHANNEL_ID on both Slack nodes to your real Slack channel ID.
5. Set Archive Defect Tag-Out Record's driveId/folderId to your real Drive location.
6. Adjust the classMaxSpeed table and remedial-day defaults in Compute FRA Speed Restriction & Remedial Timeframe if your railroad's FRA-approved track-class speeds differ from the illustrative defaults used here.

Test: submit one test segment classified Class 5 and confirm the Slack send-and-wait fires and each of approve / edit / reject correctly reaches its own Finalize node; then a Class 1-2 segment to confirm it skips the approval gate entirely.

Estimated setup time: 25-30 minutes (3 credentials, 1 endpoint URL, 1 Slack channel ID, 1 Drive folder).

**🎨 CUSTOMISATION**

1. Swap the notification channel: replace both Slack nodes with Microsoft Teams or email if your railroad's dispatch office doesn't use Slack.
2. Add an approval branch: extend the approval gate to Class 3-4 Serious segments too by widening the Requires Immediate Tag-Out? condition — currently only Class 5 requires sign-off.
3. Change the scoring model: adjust the classMaxSpeed table and the 30/180-day remedial windows in Compute FRA Speed Restriction & Remedial Timeframe to match your FDA... (FRA) Track Safety Standards edition or your railroad's own more conservative internal policy.
4. Add a second data sink: log every classified segment to Google Sheets in parallel with the Drive archive for a filterable weekly defect trend report.
5. Adapt to an adjacent vertical: the same Text-Classifier-severity → deterministic-Code → conditional-approval-gate skeleton fits bridge inspection defect triage or grade-crossing signal-defect response with a different classification schema.

**ℹ️ ADDITIONAL INFORMATION**

Error handling: every external-action node (HTTP Request, the Chat Model, the Text Classifier, both Slack nodes, Google Drive) carries onError:'continueRegularOutput' with retryOnFail:true, maxTries:3, waitBetweenTries:2000ms — a transient Slack outage while awaiting a supervisor's approval retries the send rather than losing the pending tag-out.

API cost/rate limits: one Text Classifier call per segment per day — a 40-segment short line's daily poll is ~40 OpenAI calls, comfortably within standard rate limits. Slack send-and-wait holds the execution open until the supervisor responds or the wait times out per your Slack node's own timeout setting — configure that timeout deliberately for Class 5 segments (do not leave a track segment implicitly in limbo).

Data privacy: only segment_id, track_class, and the inspector's defect notes are sent to OpenAI for classification — no personnel names or employee IDs are included in the classifier's input in this design.

Built/verified against: n8n stable as of 2026-09 (offline build — no live instance this run). Node type strings and typeVersions (incl. the Slack sendAndWait/approveAndEdit parameter shape and the 3-way Switch fallbackOutput) were offline-verified against the standing Appendix reference table and prior verified shapes; flag as Unverified for the exact Slack approval-options schema and confirm on first import.

Known limitations: this workflow assumes the inspection system returns one item per segment per day (via HTTP Request's splitIntoItems option) — a system that instead returns a single nested array will need an explicit Split Out node inserted after the fetch. Speed-restriction and remedial-timeframe values are illustrative defaults, not FRA-certified figures — your track-safety officer must confirm them against your railroad's current FRA Track Safety Standards compliance manual before production use.

Creator credit: Swapnil AI Labs — swapnil.mandloi7@gmail.com — swapnilailabs.netlify.app

nodes.name: Sticky - Poll Segments Due for Inspection

parameters.content:
**Poll Segments Due for Inspection**
Daily Schedule Trigger, 05:00.
Kicks off the whole inspection-severity sweep.
Without it nothing runs until manually triggered.

**Normalize Poll Window**
Stamps today's date and the railroad_id for the fetch call.
Keeps the rest of the workflow date-agnostic.
Single source of truth for the poll context.

nodes.name: Sticky - Fetch Segments Due & Inspector Notes

parameters.content:
**Fetch Segments Due & Inspector Notes**
GET call returning every segment due today, split into items.
URL keyed by poll_date.
The collection every downstream node processes one item at a time.

**Classifier Model**
OpenAI chat model feeding the Text Classifier.
Model: gpt-4.1-mini, temp 0.1.
Required — Text Classifier cannot run without it.

**Classify Defect Severity**
Routes each segment's inspector notes into one of 4 severity categories.
Outputs are separate branches, not a json field.
The AI reasoning step this pattern is built around.

**Tag No Defect**
Stamps defect_category='No Defect' on this output branch.
Text Classifier itself never writes this field (standing rule).
Feeds straight into the speed/remedial Code node.

**Tag Minor**
Stamps defect_category='Class 1-2 Minor'.
Monitor-only outcome, 180-day remedial window.
One of 4 mutually exclusive category branches.

**Tag Serious**
Stamps defect_category='Class 3-4 Serious'.
Triggers a real speed restriction, 30-day remedial window.
One of 4 mutually exclusive category branches.

**Tag Immediate Halt**
Stamps defect_category='Class 5 Immediate Halt'.
The only category that reaches the approval gate.
Highest-severity branch.

nodes.name: Sticky - Compute FRA Speed Restriction & Remedial Timeframe

parameters.content:
**Compute FRA Speed Restriction & Remedial Timeframe**
Real Code logic: track-class speed table + category -> mph + remedial days.
All 4 category branches converge here.
The deterministic engine behind every recommended_action.

**Requires Immediate Tag-Out?**
Branch on defect_category equals Class 5 Immediate Halt.
First of the two required real branch points.
Only this branch reaches the human approval gate.

**Shape Non-Urgent Record**
Marks approval_outcome='not_required' for non-Class-5 segments.
Skips the approval gate entirely.
Still fully archived and reported like every other outcome.

**Request Supervisor Tag-Out Approval**
Slack send-and-wait: approve / edit / reject the recommended tag-out.
This workflow's control-flow floor.
No Class 5 segment gets tagged out without this gate.

**Route Approval Response**
3-way Switch reading the Slack response payload.
Outputs: approve / edit / reject.
Second of the two required real branch points.

**Finalize Approved Tag-Out**
Stamps final_status as approved-as-recommended.
approval_outcome='approved'.
Reached only on a clean Slack approval.

**Finalize Edited Tag-Out**
Uses the supervisor's own typed text as final_status.
approval_outcome='approved_with_edit'.
Lets a human override the exact restriction on the record.

**Cancel Tag-Out (Rejected)**
Marks the tag-out rejected, sends it back for a field re-check.
approval_outcome='rejected'.
Still archived — a rejection is not a dropped record.

**Archive Defect Tag-Out Record**
Uploads the final record to Google Drive, one file per segment/day.
Runs regardless of which outcome path was taken.
Primary long-term audit sink.

**Notify Track Supervisor & Dispatch**
Posts the final category, action, and speed restriction to Slack.
Last node — closes the loop for dispatch.
Same message shape across every outcome.
